messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Example 4
Hospital course: An 81-year-old woman was brought in after a fall at home. She could not weight-bear and the right leg was shortened and externally rotated. A pelvic radiograph showed a displaced subcapital fracture of the right femoral neck. She underwent hemiarthroplasty on day one.
Answer: S72

Example 5
Hospital course: A 19-year-old man presented with 18 hours of periumbilical pain that migrated to the right iliac fossa, with anorexia and a low-grade fever. There was guarding at McBurney's point and the white cell count was 15.2. Laparoscopy confirmed an inflamed, non-perforated appendix.
Answer: K35

Example 6
Hospital course: A 64-year-old woman with a history of oestrogen-receptor-positive breast carcinoma treated five years earlier presented with progressive thoracic back pain. Magnetic resonance imaging showed deposits in T7 and T9 with no cord compression. Biopsy confirmed deposits of breast origin and she received palliative radiotherapy to the spine.
Answer: C79

Hospital course:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Patient Name: [REDACTED]
Medical Record Number: [REDACTED]

Hospital Course:
The patient, a 50-year-old Asian woman, was admitted to our hospital due to sudden anterior chest pain. Hematology, biochemistry, and blood gas analyses were performed and found to be normal. A chest computed tomography (CT) scan revealed a ground-glass opacity (GGO) in her left S10 lung segment and a solitary small nodule in her left S4 segment. Further testing was carried out, which led to suspicion of lung carcinoma. However, the patient did not provide consent for surgical resection.

After follow-up with CT scans, it was suggested that the GGO was lung carcinoma, and a pathological diagnosis was established through a left lower lobectomy and an upper lung partial resection. The cancer was identified as primary lung adenocarcinoma (localized bronchioloalveolar carcinoma).

There was also a small nodule in her left S4, which was initially suspected to be lung metastasis, however, it was later discovered to be a benign metastasizing leiomyoma (BML). The patient had a history of undergoing a total abdominal hysterectomy for uterine leiomyoma in the past, which is why the small nodule was identified as BML.

Management and Outcome:
No additional therapy was given, and the patient was monitored by follow-up chest CT scans over four years. No recurrence of lung cancer or BML could be detected throughout her follow-up.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Instructions:
The patient is advised to continue her follow-up with her physician and have periodic screening of the chest CT scans.

Scheduled Follow-up Appointments:
Follow-up screening every six months for two years and then annually.

Answer with the three-character category only.

text:
The principal diagnosis is primary lung adenocarcinoma (localized bronchioloalveolar carcinoma), treated by left lower lobectomy. In ICD-10-AM, malignant neoplasm of the bronchus or lung is category C34.

The small S4 nodule was benign metastasizing leiomyoma, which is a separate and secondary finding. The lung cancer is the condition that was surgically treated.

Answer: C34
